newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan says no sight of China spying on fighters.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan says no sight of China spying on fighters.

text.p: Taiwan said on Tuesday it had not detected any Chinese vessels spying on the island's deployment of recently-arrived fighter planes.

"After throrough investigations, so far we have yet to discover any Chinese communist fishing boats collecting information about our second-generation fighters," said Kung Fang-ting, Taiwan's defence ministry spokesman.
Kung was commenting on recent media reports that China had sent vessels to waters off Taiwan's west coast to spy on the French-made fighter jets.

The reports said vessels disguised as Chinese fishing boats, but with an unusually large number of antennae, have been seen off Taiwan's Hsinchu county near the west coast, where five recently arrived Mirage jets are to be based.
The number of vessels had increased since May 12, prompting Taiwan security authorities to suspect that they were conducting surveillance, the local China Times Express newspaper said.
The paper said the boats had not intruded into Taiwan's territorial waters, but had stayed close to the area.
Kung said the military had closely monitored various activities of the Chinese People's Liberation Army, and there was no need for the public to be worried.
Taiwan on May 5 took delivery of five of 60 Mirage jets it had ordered from France.

It also took delivery on May 15 of three more U.S. F-16 fighter jets which, together with two that arrived in April, were expected to strengthen Taiwan's air force combat power in the face of continued military threats from arch-rival China.

Taiwan in 1992 bought 150 F-16s from the United States and 60 Mirages from France in deals that outraged China, which views the island as a rebel-held province subject to eventual reunification with the mainland.
China has threatened to attack Taiwan, which split from the mainland at the end of a civil war in 1949, if the island tries to declare formal independence.
